clue.text: Heavy food awkward to digest without it

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsily arranged, so these letters are to be reshuffled
the letters of the word it must be left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A warning that some heavy food is hard on the stomach unless something is avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of TO DIGEST, shuffled ('awkward'), make the answer plus IT, which 'without' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is filling, starchy food that sits heavily in the stomach.

clue.text: Body of soldiers, tense, without means to ascend

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: having no money is being poor

explanation.surface: A tense, penniless group of soldiers trying to climb in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ascend' turns POOR upward in this down entry, giving ROOP under T.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, especially of cavalry or armour.

clue.text: Put off by fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged by a fellow who cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, such as washing powder or liquid.

clue.text: Rates unusual zircon, initially, as imitation

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters signals that they are shuffled
initially points to the opening letter of the word zircon

explanation.surface: A jeweller pricing an odd zircon as a fake diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges RATES to ERSAT; 'initially' gives Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a substitute or artificial version, typically inferior to the real thing.

clue.text: Day of celebration perhaps, in flats I've renovated

indicators.note: renovated flats are remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A housewarming party held in some newly done-up apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges FLATSIVE. 'perhaps' marks a festival as only one kind of celebration day.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is an occasion of public celebration, often a holy day or feast.

clue.text: Lose it, knowing of article supporting female name

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the article comes after the female letter

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp
the is the definite article
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A wise remark on a woman's name supported by a 'the'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' sets THE below F in the down entry. FLY means street-smart in British slang; HANDLE is a nickname or name.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off the handle is an idiom for suddenly losing your temper.

clue.text: Loud type of jazz music — name trio's leader

parts.note: stride is a style of jazz piano

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of trio's is taken

explanation.surface: A noisy jazz trio introduced by its frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T from trio's. Stride is a rhythmic jazz piano style from 1920s Harlem.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means harsh and loud, as in a strident voice.

clue.text: Turn of phrase I love about Diane and Mike

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
Di is a short form of Diane
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A romantic line: I love Diane, and also Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and O around DI, giving IDIO, before M.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression whose meaning cannot be worked out from its words, a fixed phrase.

clue.text: Inherited a northern castle? Oddly, that's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next piece
oddly suggests things set out strangely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A northern castle passed down the family, with something odd about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges CASTLE to CESTAL, and 'about' puts that round R to make CESTRAL after A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral things are handed down from forebears, so they are inherited.

clue.text: Speak, interrupting very different type of prophet

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: something interrupting cuts into another, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: other means different
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: A seer breaking into a conversation, a very different kind of prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very different' reads as one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces; 'interrupting' splits the second of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer foretells the future, a kind of prophet or seer.

clue.text: Measure some chinchillas

indicators.note: some means only a part of the word chinchillas is taken

explanation.surface: Weighing or sizing up a few chinchillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the letters from inside chINCHillas.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, a measure of twelve to the foot.

clue.text: Drink Italian provided after a rep returned

indicators.note: after places the following pieces later in the answer than the ones before
something returned comes back the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)
if means provided, as a condition

explanation.surface: A sales rep, back in the office, demanding a drink from an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' gives IT as in gin and It, the Italian vermouth; 'after' places the Italian and the proviso behind the returned rep.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: US prosecutor needs to disguise material

parts.note: DA is the District Attorney, an American public prosecutor
to mask is to disguise

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor going undercover in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a figured woven fabric, typically of silk or linen.

clue.text: Record temperature, then take off

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic or take them off

explanation.surface: Log the temperature, then depart, as with a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like leaving but means to imitate, as in a comic impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Reparation from that one mentioned

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Amends sought for something that person spoke of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of thAT ONE MENTioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, a form of reparation.

clue.text: Cooking method, first of three broadcast on radio

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word three
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A cookery programme heard on the wireless, the opening episode of three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast on radio' looks like a sound clue, but 'broadcast' rearranges ON RADIO to ANDOORI after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori cooking bakes or roasts food in a tandoor, a clay oven used in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Form of government that may make one go charily

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters can be formed into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regime so oppressive that it makes people step warily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges GO CHARILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchy is rule by a small group of people, a type of government.

clue.text: Face endless people giving a torrent of abuse

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, and also slang for a person's face
a tribe is a people or group

explanation.surface: Confronting a group that keeps hurling insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the L of DIAL, leaving DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a sustained stream of criticism.

clue.text: Sorry tale about legal document excluding women

indicators.note: about means going around, so the tale surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a conte is a short story or tale

indicators.note: excluding means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a writ is a written court order

explanation.surface: A regretful story about a legal paper that left out women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tale' gives the French-derived word conte, a short story; 'excluding' and 'about' then work on the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling remorse, genuinely apologetic for a wrong.

clue.text: Papers produced by the French unemployed

parts.note: ID is identification papers
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Documents produced in France by someone out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can describe someone without work, not employed.

clue.text: Comic circulating an unfounded rumour

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a card is a funny or eccentric person, a comic

explanation.surface: A comedian spreading a baseless story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like an adjective or a magazine, but is a noun for a funny person, a card; 'circulating' sends it round the word an.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or hoax, a groundless story.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

definitions.meaning: to desert to the opposing side (verb)

explanation.surface: Losing the battle, so going over to the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Defect is a noun for a fault and a verb for abandoning one's country or party for another.

clue.text: Course record therefore momentous, originally

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
so means therefore

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word momentous

explanation.surface: A historic lap record, therefore momentous.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a course, and Epsom Downs is a famous one.

clue.text: Sort of menu left next to a trolley in A&E

indicators.note: in means the pieces are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: A&E is a British hospital's Accident and Emergency department; its letters A and E go around
a cart is a trolley

explanation.surface: A hospital menu left on a trolley in Accident and Emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L, A and CART between the A and E of A&E, the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: A la carte describes a menu priced dish by dish rather than as a set meal.

clue.text: Ceasefire, short, set up on base

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised and read from the bottom

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A brief truce agreed at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CURT upward to TRUC; 'on' puts it above E in the down entry. The mathematical constant e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting for a time.

clue.text: Dog's breakfast in canteen

definitions.meaning: a dog's breakfast is British slang for a ..., a muddle
a military dining hall, a canteen

explanation.surface: Feeding the dog in the cafeteria.
explanation.definitionFit: Mess means both a chaotic muddle and the place where service personnel eat.

clue.text: One may be used to exercise in Delhi gym, maybe

definitions.text: One may be used to exercise

parts.note: Delhi is in India, so anything from there is Indian
a gym is one kind of club, a health club

explanation.surface: Something you might use to work out at a fitness centre in Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym, maybe' gives CLUB, a gym being one example of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian club is a bottle-shaped wooden club swung in exercise routines.

clue.text: Impressed by energy charge

parts.note: impressed means stamped, as with a mark pressed in
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Bowled over by someone's vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush of animals or people, a charge.

clue.text: Poet in dreary study

parts.note: dry can mean dull or dreary, as of a dry lecture
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A writer of verse in a dull reading room.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden is a famous English poet, so the answer is an example of a poet.
